race.name: Gran Fondo Mendoza
race.tagline: A fast 110-kilometer circuit climbs from central Mendoza toward Cacheuta, with 1,185 meters of gain under the Andes.

vitals.field_size: Second edition; no verified field count published
vitals.start_format: Chip-timed category start groups; staging 06:30-07:00 and scheduled start 07:15
vitals.registration: 2027 registration is open through the official event site
vitals.entry_fee: Launch pricing: ARS 160,000 Gran Fondo / ARS 120,000 Medio Fondo; organizer says prices may change
vitals.feed_zones: Three hydration stations, or more at organizer discretion, with water, fruit, and snacks
vitals.cutoff_time: A closing vehicle removes riders it catches from event support; final time and location details may change in organizer updates
route_options: Gran Fondo: marketed as 110 km; organizer-linked route file is 109.6 km / 1,185 m climbing
Medio Fondo: marketed as 50 km; organizer-linked route file is 41.7 km / 401 m climbing

climate.description: March in Mendoza can still be warm and exposed. The long circuit moves from the city toward the Andes foothills, where sun, dry air, and wind can amplify hydration mistakes.

terrain.primary: Paved rolling circuit with one sustained foothill sector
terrain.surface: Organizer-linked route data identifies a fully paved road course through Mendoza, Lujan de Cuyo, and Cacheuta.
features: Vineyard roads through Lujan de Cuyo

fondo_rating.scoring_notes: The organizer supplies a competitive 2027 rulebook, chip timing, classifications, route files, aid, medical support, and a city-center start. The Andes setting is strong, but the event is only entering its second edition and its 110-kilometer course is moderate rather than monumental, producing a cautious Tier 3 grade.

key_climbs: The outbound rise from Lujan de Cuyo toward Cacheuta
climb_profile.king_of_mountain: The gradual Cacheuta approach is the course's main energy-management problem rather than a single categorized summit.

course_description.character: The 2027 Gran Fondo targets the organizer-linked 109.6-kilometer paved circuit from Mendoza toward Lujan de Cuyo and Cacheuta. The first half rewards efficient group riding; the cumulative 1,185 meters and foothill exposure make restraint important before the descending return. It is a road-racing durability problem with a meaningful climbing middle, not an Alpine summit event.
course_description.signature_challenge: Holding efficient pressure toward Cacheuta without spending the legs needed for the fast return to Mendoza.

logistics.airport: Governor Francisco Gabrielli International Airport (MDZ) is roughly 10 kilometers from central Mendoza.
logistics.lodging_strategy: Stay in central Mendoza near the organizer's final accreditation and start instructions; the current homepage and rulebook name different central staging points, so final rider communications override both.
logistics.transport: Accreditation and expo are scheduled for Saturday, March 13. The organizer requires in-person number pickup and does not issue numbers on race morning.
logistics.food: Registration includes on-course water, fruit, and snacks plus food and drink at the finish; riders must carry their own bottles.

history.origin_story: Gran Fondo Mendoza launched as a competitive road event connecting Argentina's major wine city with the Andes foothills and Cacheuta.
notable_moments: 2026: Inaugural edition established the Mendoza-Cacheuta circuit
2027: Second edition scheduled for March 14 with Gran and Medio distances
history.reputation: A new regional gran fondo with unusually complete first-party 2027 documentation, but too little operating history to claim established-event prestige.

biased_opinion.verdict: The Andes Backdrop Is Better Than the Palmares—For Now
biased_opinion.summary: Mendoza has the ingredients for a worthwhile early-season target: a real timed race, a legible 110-kilometer course, enough climbing to punish sloppy pacing, and a distinctive wine-country-to-foothills setting. The restraint is history: this is a second edition, not yet a proven international fondo.
weaknesses: Homepage and rulebook conflict on the precise start point
biased_opinion.bottom_line: Race it for a compact, competitive Argentine objective with a strong setting; do not mistake the scenery for the history of a mature bucket-list fondo.

final_verdict.one_liner: A fast 110-kilometer circuit climbs from central Mendoza toward Cacheuta, with 1,185 meters of gain under the Andes.
final_verdict.should_you_race: Yes if you want a documented, chip-timed South American race with moderate climbing and simple city logistics; wait if proven execution and a deep international field are essential.
final_verdict.alternatives: GFNY Villavicencio for a more climbing-focused Colombian race, or Gran Fondo Argentina for a more established domestic event.
